acceptance: FROZEN BEFORE THE RE-RUN. This round re-executes, from the current reproducible state, the verifications that were previously done as pre-admission exploratory work; the exploratory artifacts are labelled as such in problems/MATH-001/experiments/EXPLORATORY_WORK.md and only results produced inside this round are recorded below. Acceptance criteria, fixed now: (A1) RE-VALIDATE the third independent certificate checker by re-running the adversarial suite (positive controls, deliberate collinear negative, duplicate, out-of-range, count error, randomised fuzz with a no-shared-code oracle) and require zero oracle/verifier disagreements and both verdict directions exercised; (A2) RE-DERIVE exact small-n ground truth by full powerset enumeration n=1..4 WITHOUT the 2n row bound, and by exhaustive row-pair enumeration n=2..8, and require the two methods to agree where they overlap; (A3) RE-VERIFY all 36,912 configurations of the 1997 corpus and require 0 failures, plus the mutation teeth check requiring every decode-invariant-preserving mutation to become illegal; (A4) RE-VERIFY the complete all_known_solutions corpus (431,008 configurations) and require 0 failures, and confirm n=75 is the only n in [2,76] with zero configurations; (A5) RE-VERIFY the n=71,72,73,74,76 record constructions through BOTH independent retrieval paths and require the decoded point sets to be identical; (A6) RE-RUN the n=75 bench calibration (cell and orbit formulations against exhaustive ground truth, plus UNSAT controls) and require 0 failures; (A7) RE-RUN the CNF completeness audit and the DRAT precondition test, requiring the new fail-closed regression suites to pass and the DRAT test to report the honest blocked status with a non-zero exit. FAILURE HANDLING, fixed now: any criterion that does not hold is recorded as a failure in the result; none of the acceptance criteria may be relaxed after the run. No claim about D(n) for any n, and no UNSAT claim, may be derived from this round beyond what a verified certificate supports.
not_done: Not attempted in this round and therefore NOT claimed: Lean formalization; a local-search/MCTS arm; an n=75 solver run (the compute phase remains COMPUTE_REQUIRED); any DRAT/LRAT certificate (the environment cannot certify an UNSAT -- see n75_attack/COMPUTE_PHASE_PROTOCOL.md G4 and the DRAT precondition test); any statement about D(n) for an n without a verified certificate; the general conjecture. The exploratory literature audit and PR reviews are not round products and are not re-registered here. Third-party corpora are not committed (see lit_data/THIRD_PARTY_SOURCES.md); the round re-run fetches and hash-verifies them.

preflight.limitations: Bounded search: 4 queries spanning the four categories plus direct retrieval of the primary sources. Adjacent-scope items were read at abstract level only. One search returned claims directly contradicted by primary retrieval and is recorded as such rather than relied on. A search returning nothing is not a proof of openness. No paid literature was consulted.
preflight.scope_comparison: Card scope: existence of D(n)=2n for all n>=2, or a rigorous counterexample or general bound. No same-scope solution and no counterexample exists. Explicitly NOT answers to this problem: (a) finite certificates establish D(n)=2n for one n only; (b) arXiv:2607.05255 resolves the no-(k+1)-in-line problem for k>=3 and leaves k=2 open; (c) the Guy-Kelly/Voutier work concerns the asymptotic COUNT of solutions, not D(n); (d) the absence of an n=75 configuration in a database is a search-status fact, not an impossibility result.
preflight.baseline: Baseline for this round = the exploratory artifacts being re-executed, plus the external corpora: (a) the third independent checker with its adversarial suite; (b) exhaustive small-n ground truth (powerset n<=4 without the 2n bound; row-pair n=2..8); (c) the 36,912-configuration 1997 corpus and the 431,008-configuration complete corpus, both fetched and hash-verified at run time; (d) the live lookup endpoint as the second retrieval path for the n=71..76 records.
